newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian Semperit workers vow to fight job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Semperit workers vow to fight job cuts.

text.p: Workers at Austrian tyre maker Semperit vowed on Monday to continue their fight to save jobs at the plant and prevent German owners Continental from transferring production to the Czech Republic.
Around 600 workers at a union meeting voted to obstruct the planned removal of machinery from the Traiskirchen plant in Lower Austria, Austrian news agency APA reported.
"If blocking the way does not do the trick, we are ready to tie ourselves to the machines," APA quoted workers' council chairman Rudolf Neubauer as saying.
Continental has said it will halve car tyre production in Traiskirchen and shed more than a thousand jobs.
Over the next few weeks the firm will begin transferring machinery to Barum in the Czech Republic, where labour costs are significantly lower.

By the end of 1997 Semperit's workforce will be halved to 1,200 and car tyre output will drop to two million annually from four million. Tyre production for heavy goods vehicles will remain at 500,000 a year.
Austrian radio said a final vote on possible industrial action would be taken in two weeks, when all of the firm's workers have returned from their summer break.
Austrian politicians, including Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, intervened in recent months to try and save Austrian jobs.
"(Continental's) arguments are not convincing...Austria is not a nation of overly high labour costs," Vranitzky said in a statement at the weekend.

"It is important to support the Semperit workforce, not as an isolated case but as an important symbol...We must defend Austria's industrial interests." -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
